title: Influencers in Mexico work for drug groups

paragraphs: Ever since the Sinaloa Cartel split into rival groups in 2024, social media has turned into a dangerous battleground for Mexico’s drug wars.

The competing factions regularly target popular content creators, and use them to show off power, post propaganda, and recruit young people. Local influencers who adopt narco culture for clicks often get caught in the middle and put themselves directly in the sights of rival gangs. On top of that, federal agents are looking into dozens of creators accused of helping cartels clean dirty money through online shops, brand deals, and live donations.

This deadly connection has already cost the lives of at least 19 influencers across the country. Weak police work, a lack of real punishment, and slow moderation by tech platforms mean cartels can keep using young creators as easy tools for cash and influence online.

paragraphs: In Mexico, social media is a dangerous battleground for drug cartels. Since a big cartel split into fighting groups in 2024, criminal gangs use popular influencers for propaganda, showing off power, and attracting young members.
At least 19 internet stars died after being linked to criminal organizations.

Some influencers make videos about drug culture for clicks, while others are investigated for helping cartels clean illegal money through private businesses and shops. Police struggle to stop the violence, and very few murders are ever solved.
Social media companies try to ban bad profiles, but cartels use hidden codes to break rules. As a result, young influencers are still in danger.

paragraphs: Drug gangs in Mexico are using social media. They want to show off and fight each other.

Back in 2024, a big gang breaks into two groups. Now, they are fighting for control. They use young online stars to make videos and bring in new people. But this is very dangerous. At least 19 creators die. Some creators talk about gang life only to get views. Others help hide dirty money in normal businesses.
The police do not stop the killers. The danger keeps growing. Social media companies try to block bad accounts, but it is not enough to keep young people safe.
